_about: Project-specific facts the gate scripts read. The scripts themselves name no
table, column, tier, side file or number prefix; everything of that kind is
here. CI copies this file next to the base-branch gate copies (/tmp/gate),
so a pull request cannot change the gate it is judged by. Any change to
this file is a bar move (history-audit).
Tests of the gate scripts, by exact path. CI runs them first, before any
code a worker wrote, from a copy of the tree whose tests/ holds only these
files, their fixtures and mutation probes, and which has no src/: worker
branches may write tests/** and src/**, and a module (or a native
extension) there could otherwise change what these tests check. None of
them may import src/. A pull request is judged by the union of this list
on the base branch and on its own head, so a change cannot drop a test.
The files are gate files (history-audit).
G2P or other tool predictions loaded into a temporary copy of the corpus
before a side's SQL is replayed. The copy is never written under data/.
A brief's ```pred fence lists one stem per line; the file is
<stem>.jsonl under dirs[side] and the table is table_prefix + stem.
id joins join_table.join_column. dup_prefix is the same prefix relations
applies to corpus keys when it doubles the corpus.
Branch classes for scope_check.py. Match order is the list order of
'classes': the first regex that matches names the class. An agent branch
carries a task id and a role; the role's write set is the only thing it
may touch ({task} is the task id from the branch name). A non-role class's
allow may also use {task}, taken from the named group in its match.
Owner-only classes need the pull-request author on the owner allowlist.
Protected paths include the agent instructions Cursor loads into every
Cloud Agent: .cursor/, .agents/, .claude/ and .codex/ at any depth (the
bare name too, which catches a symlink standing in for the directory),
and every AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .cursorrules.
Every commit in a pull request must have an author and a committer
email from this list, or the GitHub noreply address of a repository
owner ((<id>+)<owner>@users.noreply.github.com). GitHub credits a
commit to whichever account owns its email, so a made-up identity such
as Tom <tom@users.noreply.github.com> lists a stranger as a
contributor. noreply@github.com covers commits GitHub itself makes
(merges, Update branch, web edits).
